item.title: Vance to host Congress at White House to discuss legislative action on healthcare fraud
item.description: Vice President JD Vance will host roughly 20 members of Congress at the White House to discuss legislative action targeting Medicare and Medicaid fraud.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Vice President JD Vance will host members of Congress at the White House on Wednesday morning for a fraud task force meeting where members will discuss potential legislative action to address the administration’s crackdown on fraud.

A source familiar with the meeting told Fox News Digital that roughly 20 members from both the House and Senate are expected at the meeting. Vance will also detail how members can target fraud in the various states and districts they represent.

Vance has previously hosted meetings at the White House to address fraud with a number of attorneys general alongside other members from the administration involved in the task force led by Vance.

PENNSYLVANIA AG EXPLAINS WHY STATE LEADS NATION IN MEDICAID FRAUD CONVICTIONS WHILE OTHERS BATTLE MASS SCHEMES

"Our task force is using every tool at its disposal to end fraud once and for all. Congress has an important role to play in cracking down on fraudsters and protecting federal programs from abuse," a White House official told Fox News Digital. "President Trump, Vice President Vance, and all of the task force’s interagency partners will not relent until every fraudster is brought to justice."

On Tuesday, the Justice Department announced that it is expanding its Northeast Health Care Fraud Strike Force to Philadelphia as federal and state authorities target alleged Medicare and Medicaid fraud involving home healthcare services, adding Pennsylvania to a number of states across the country where the administration is honed in on fraud.

Federal and state law enforcement charged 19 defendants accused of participating in schemes involving more than $4 million in claims submitted to Medicare and Medicaid, according to a DOJ release obtained by Fox News.

On Sunday, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday also announced a plea agreement involving the final defendant in a previously charged 21-defendant case tied to more than $1.7 million in claims.

"The vice president’s task force continues to stop the flow of taxpayer funds before they fall into the hands of fraudsters and deliver savings to the American people," a spokesperson for Vice President JD Vance told Fox News Digital. "This is great momentum in the fight for the President’s War on Fraud."

WATCH: DR. OZ SAYS NEWSOM, OTHER BLUE STATES HAVE TURNED MEDICAID FRAUD INTO A 'FEATURE'

The task force has suspended payments to a number of healthcare providers who have been suspected of fraud across the country. As of May, Vance and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz withheld more than $1.4 billion in federal funding for home health and hospice providers nationwide.

In June, the Trump administration revealed new figures that show a drastic 7,100% spike in Medicare claims for skin substitutes in just six years, surging from $200 million to $14.4 billion from 2019 to 2025.

CMS identified 4,200 suspicious claims for skin substitutes, known as allografts, totaling $224 million in charges through May of this year.

"That's a lot of money," Oz said during a news conference in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on Wednesday. "And that bankrupts not just hospital systems and physician groups, but it causes major problems across the entire landscape."

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT’S LANDLORD JOINS VANCE FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE WIDENS HUNT: 'CRITICAL FORCE'

President Donald Trump established the task force through an executive order in May. He appointed Vance to the fraud crackdown team and various agencies and departments have been involved in rooting out widespread fraud.

"Vice President JD Vance and Republicans are doing a great job hunting down Fraud in the various States," Trump posted on Truth Social in June. "Billions of Dollars is being found, and we've just started!"

item.title: Wisconsin brewery that promised free beer when Trump dies now plans 'half-price beer day' when McConnell dies
item.description: Minocqua Brewing Company announced half-price beer when Sen. Mitch McConnell dies, blaming the Kentucky Republican for half of America's problems.
item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin brewery that previously sparked outrage by promising free beer on "the day" President Donald Trump dies is once again drawing criticism after announcing plans for a "half-price beer day" when Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., dies.

In a post on Instagram on Monday, Minocqua Brewing Company said it plans to celebrate McConnell's death by offering beer at half price, arguing the longtime Kentucky Republican was responsible for "about half of all America's current problems."

"Well, folks, if our logic is right, we're supposed to get the news today that ‘Rigor Tortoise’ kicked the bucket about two months ago," the brewery said.

'THIS IS NOT NORMAL': AOC UNLOADS ON MCCONNELL'S PROLONGED ABSENCE

"Why today? Because so-called 'Establishment Democratic Hero' and modern day gutless member of the do-nothing opposition party — Governor Andy Beshear — failed to call a special election to replace the ‘ghost from Kentucky’ before August 3rd — which means by Kentucky law, the seat will go unfilled until January."

"When they announce that McConnell's Faustian dance has finally ended, we're gonna start serving our beer at ‘half price,’ because we promised #halfpricebeerday on the day they unplug the ventilator," the brewery continued.

McConnell, who is 84, has not been in the Senate for more than a month after being hospitalized for a fall in his home.

Last week, Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear demanded that McConnell prove he is fit to continue serving in Congress after a lengthy hospital stay or resign from office.

"I am calling on you to directly and verbally address the people of Kentucky and provide proof of your capacity to serve, or resign," Beshear wrote in a letter to McConnell, obtained by Fox News Digital.

WISCONSIN DEM'S BAR LAMENTS 'WE ALMOST GOT FREE BEER DAY' FOR TRUMP ASSASSINATION

In the post, the brewery said it chose the name "half-price beer day" because it blamed McConnell for "about half" of the country's current problems while noting that its previously announced "free beer day" promotion remained reserved for "someone more special."

The brewery also promoted "half-price beer day" T-shirts and encouraged supporters to wear them when the event eventually takes place.

Minocqua Brewing Company, which in a January social media post appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, while not explicitly using his name, is currently fighting getting their permit revoked.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on July 27 that Wisconsin's Department of Revenue sent a notice to liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad announcing plans to revoke the brewery’s permit.

'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The paper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

The revocation of the beer permit was set to go into effect on Tuesday, but a spokesperson for Wisconsin's Department of Revenue told Fox News Digital in a statement that "Minocqua Brewing Company has filed an administrative appeal, and, therefore, the permit will not be revoked, pending the outcome of the administrative appeal."

Bangstad, the owner of the brewery, is also the founder of the Minocqua Brewing Company SuperPAC, which "aims to remove Republican federal and state elected officials who perpetuated the election lies that caused the Insurrection of January 6, 2021, and whose downplaying of the seriousness of COVID-19 caused so many unnecessary deaths in our country," according to the brewery’s website.

Fox News Digital reached out to Minocqua Brewing Company, Gov. Beshear's office and Sen. McConnell's office for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

item.title: Washington wildfire arson suspect previously charged with first-degree murder, records show
item.description: Aaron Farinacci, charged with first-degree arson in Spokane's Old Trails Fire, previously pleaded guilty to manslaughter in a 2010 Arizona homicide.
item.content:encoded:
The man accused of setting the largest of the wildfires that have destroyed hundreds of buildings and forced tens of thousands of people from their homes in eastern Washington was previously charged with first-degree murder before pleading guilty to a reduced manslaughter charge, court records show.

Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, was arrested Monday on suspicion of first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire, the largest of three blazes burning in and around Spokane, Washington's second-largest city.

The fires have destroyed at least 700 buildings and forced about 67,000 people to evacuate. Authorities have not alleged any connection between Farinacci and the other two fires, which remain under investigation.

WASHINGTON MAN ARRESTED ON ARSON CHARGE TIED TO DEVASTATING SPOKANE WILDFIRE

The arrest came hours after Washington Gov. Jay Inslee, a Democrat, pointed to climate change as firefighters battled the region's destructive wildfires.

"Climate change isn't some existential global thing," Inslee said Monday. "It's our neighbors. It's our friends."

Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Farinacci was initially charged with first-degree murder and aggravated assault in a 2010 Arizona homicide before pleading guilty in 2012 to reduced charges of manslaughter and aggravated assault.

The Associated Press reported that Farinacci, then 21, fatally shot his father during an argument over washing dishes in Mesa, Arizona, in 2010. Farinacci also shot himself but survived.

A Maricopa County judge sentenced Farinacci to 12 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to manslaughter and aggravated assault. Arizona Department of Corrections records show he was released on Dec. 23, 2020.

Less than six years after his release from prison, Farinacci again found himself accused of a major crime.

The Spokane County Sheriff's Office said Major Crimes detectives and Washington State Department of Natural Resources fire investigators identified Farinacci as the suspect after developing probable cause during the investigation.

Detectives obtained arrest and search warrants before taking Farinacci into custody without incident at his Spokane residence, where he was booked into the Spokane County Jail on suspicion of first-degree arson.

Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said witnesses reported seeing a man – later identified as Farinacci – acting suspiciously near where the fire started. After returning home and noticing smoke rising from the same area, they flagged down an Airway Heights police officer and provided investigators with a physical description of the man and the clothing he was wearing.

Deputies initially detained and questioned Farinacci before releasing him as first responders focused on evacuating residents threatened by the rapidly growing fire, Nowels said.

When deputies first contacted Farinacci, he was carrying waterproof matches and a butane lighter, investigators said. Fire investigators later determined the blaze was consistent with dry grass being ignited by a match or lighter.

The sheriff credited observant residents with helping investigators quickly identify the suspect.

item.title: New York police official accused of driving getaway car for son in gang-related shooting
item.description: Jennifer Lackard, a Mount Vernon deputy police commissioner, allegedly sped off with her son Chase after he shot at rival gang members near Bronx court.
item.content:encoded:
A New York police official is being accused of serving as the getaway driver for her son in an apparent gang shooting in New York City, the New York Post reported Tuesday.

Police sources told the Post that Jennifer Lackard, a deputy police commissioner with the Mount Vernon Police Department, was arrested along with her son, Chase Lackard, 20, at their home Tuesday morning. Authorities said Chase was charged with shooting at rival gang members near the Bronx Criminal Court in late June.

Sources told the Post that Chase ran to his mother in her car after the shooting, and she sped off.

No one was injured in the shooting.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

Both the mother and son have been charged with attempted murder, attempted assault, criminal possession of a firearm, conspiracy and reckless endangerment.

The Mount Vernon Police Department said Tuesday that Lackard had been terminated effectively immediately.

"The allegations are unrelated to her duties with the Mount Vernon Police Department and do not stem from any conduct associated with the Department or the performance of her official responsibilities," the department wrote on social media.

ROMANIAN NATIONAL LEARNS FATE FOR SWATTING US OFFICIALS, INCLUDING MEMBERS OF CONGRESS, JUDGES

The incident was far from Chase's first run-in with law enforcement. He was shot by police in 2024 after allegedly wielding a gun during an argument.

He was also shot once before in 2023 by three other youths during a dispute on a bus. Chase is allegedly a member of the "Slutty Gang," according to the Post.

He reportedly demanded to know what gang the other youths belonged to and then attempted to drag one of them off the bus before being shot in the chest.

item.title: Embattled GOP rep takes dramatic step to 'clear my name' as abuse allegations engulf House race
item.description: Rep. Max Miller filed for an ethics investigation into himself to clear his name as Sen. Bernie Moreno calls him a "danger" to his own family.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, is calling for an investigation into abuse allegations made against him by his ex-wife, as the dramatic family feud overshadows his race for re-election.

Miller has consistently denied wrongdoing and accused both his ex-wife and her father, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, of trying to take down his political career.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs, I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and my family. I have absolutely nothing to hide," Miller wrote on X on Tuesday.

"We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

OHIO GOP FAMILY FEUD EXPLODES AS SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS ON REP MAX MILLER TO RESIGN

The Ethics Committee confirmed on Tuesday afternoon that it would investigate allegations that Miller "may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use."

Emily Moreno, who filed for divorce from Miller in 2024 after two years of marriage, has accused him of physically abusing both her and their young daughter. Allegations include that he scalded Moreno with boiling water and held a gun to her head during two separate occasions, and that she had to get their daughter medical aid for a broken collar bone after she was in Miller's care.

Miller suggested in a livestream on X over the weekend that Moreno had suffered from mental health issues in the past and that might be the reason behind her accusations. He also said none of the allegations she made have been substantiated by relevant entities.

"Every single one of these allegations were already investigated. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me," Miller said in the video. He said the water incident occurred during "horseplay" between the two, and disputed that the water was boiling. He also said Moreno took their daughter to the emergency room thinking there was a bruise on their daughter's neck, but that the mark was from finger painting.

SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS FOR EX-SON-IN-LAW TO RESIGN FROM HOUSE, GET 'SERIOUS PSYCHOLOGICAL HELP'

But mounting public pressure has brought the Cleveland-area feud to Washington, where Sen. Moreno told reporters Tuesday that Miller "fails to meet that minimum basic standard" for elected officials who get to serve.

He also criticized Miller in a statement posted on X, calling him a "danger" to his daughter and granddaughter. Miller and Moreno share custody over the child.

The intense public scrutiny is also potentially putting Miller's re-election into question, with Democrats seeing new opportunity in what was a relatively safe red seat in the Cleveland suburbs.

One House GOP source, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about a sensitive situation, told Fox News Digital the situation was a "f—-ing trainwreck."

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

The source noted that the allegations against Miller had not been substantiated, but said "the court of public opinion is a b—-."

Miller likely appears to voters to have "a little too much on his plate," the source said.

Meanwhile, a House Republican, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly, said Miller should not run for re-election. "We must lead by example," they said.

The same House Republican also called for Reps. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., and Cory Mills, R-Fla., also facing harassment allegations that they have denied, to similarly drop out of their races.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But Miller has been defiant so far, expressing confidence that he'll win in November.

The House Ethics Committee, which Miller is calling on to investigate his case, recently recommended that Edwards be censured for his behavior toward two young female staffers.

item.title: Devastated mother blames soft-on-crime policies after career criminal is charged in son’s death
item.description: Jacob Freytes' family pushes for mandatory life sentences for child killers after the 12-year-old was fatally struck by a stray bullet in the Bronx.
item.content:encoded:
The family of a 12-year-old boy killed by a stray bullet in the Bronx is demanding change after a suspect with a lengthy arrest record was charged with his murder.

After the death of Jacob Freytes, the son of a retired NYPD detective sergeant, his mother and sister are pushing for "Jacob's Law," which they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child's life.

"I gave him a kiss, and I walked out, and we always do a little dolphin kiss. And I walked out and went to work," Migdalia Martinez, Freytes' mother, told "Fox & Friends" Tuesday.

2 DETAINED AFTER SHOOTING IN NEW YORK LEAVES 15-YEAR-OLD KILLED, TWO OTHERS WOUNDED: POLICE

"Around five o'clock, they called me and said that he had gotten shot. And all I could do was try to think of different ways to get here faster," she added. "When I got there, I just seen my boy gone."

Freytes, who was riding his bike to a nearby bodega to buy a ball, was shot and killed after a suspect opened fire during an alleged street dispute. Two other adults were also wounded in the shooting.

Police said William Ferrer, 45, was arrested and faces multiple charges, including second-degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty. Ferrer has an arrest record dating back more than 25 years, including prior charges for drunk driving, drug possession, menacing and criminal contempt, according to the New York Post.

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch addressed Ferrer’s arrest on X, writing, "Jacob was an innocent bystander on his bike when he was taken from his family yesterday in an act of senseless gun violence.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

"No arrest can ever ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, but the NYPD will continue to do everything in our power to seek justice for Jacob."

The family is calling for a proposed "Jacob's Law" that they say would require life sentences for people convicted of recklessly taking a child’s life. The family also criticized New York's crime policies, including cash bail reforms for misdemeanors and the end of stop-and-frisk.

"It's just so much that they allow that, at this point, it's just safer more for the criminals than it is for hardworking people," Martinez said.

Freytes’ sister, Angelica Coriano, said the family welcomed the charges but remained uneasy about whether the suspect would receive enough prison time if convicted.

LOUISIANA BILL EXPANDS FIRST-DEGREE MURDER CHARGES AND DEATH PENALTY ELIGIBILITY AFTER MALL SHOOTING

"'Jacob's Law' will allow for there to be no in-between whether somebody goes to jail or not for taking a child's life recklessly. It'll allow for criminals to go straight to jail or prison instead of the family having to go to court continuously hoping and wondering if they're [going to] get the justice that they deserve for the child that they lost," Coriano said.

"And we went to court and found out all the charges that he'd be receiving, which is great, but we still have to sit with the worry whether he'll face all the time that is necessary enough to keep him where he needs to be. And that type of uncertainty is very uncomfortable for us as a family, knowing that we'll never see our child again."

Martinez remembered her son as a "funny, quirky kid" who loved his friends, family and playing video games. 

"There wasn't an old woman he didn't help with bags or cross the street," she said. "There wasn't a person that if he caught your eye, he'd make sure to tell you hi."

item.title: Angel Reese got a Barbie doll, signature shoe and WNBA theme night, then played victim again
item.description: Angel Reese's new Barbie doll and signature sneaker cap a 10-day stretch of promotions, but her comments about representation raise questions.
item.content:encoded:
Angel Reese just wrapped up an extraordinary 10-day stretch that most young girls in America could only dream about.

On July 24, Mattel unveiled a Barbie doll made in her likeness. The doll wore a pink jersey featuring Reese’s No. 5, the number she wears with the Atlanta Dream, and included details such as her headband, leg sleeve, necklace, pink nails and signature Reebok shoes.

On July 25, she competed in her third consecutive WNBA All-Star Game.

On Aug. 3, a matching Barbie edition of the Angel Reese 1, her signature sneaker, went on sale.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

That same night, the Dream held "Barbie Game Day" at State Farm Arena, complete with special ticket packages and limited-edition merchandise. Reese’s doll sat beside her during media availability.

In 10 days, Reese received her own Barbie, a matching version of her signature shoe and an entire WNBA promotional event tied to the collaboration.

Yet even that wasn’t enough to keep Reese from returning to her favorite subject: what the world had denied her.

"Honestly, I didn’t have a lot of dolls because I didn’t have dolls that really looked like me much," Reese said when asked what dolls she played with growing up.

"That’s why I kind of really wanted to make sure this was super intentional, because now that they have a doll that looks like you, nails and hair, but also you can be a killer on the court as well."

Reese didn’t say Black dolls never existed, but she clearly framed her childhood doll options as a failure of representation.

So, it's worth noting that Mattel introduced Christie, a Black character in Barbie’s world, in 1968. The first doll officially named Black Barbie arrived in 1980, more than two decades before Reese was born. American Girl introduced Addy Walker in 1993.

And in 1998, Mattel sold officially licensed African-American NBA Barbie dolls wearing authentic team uniforms and packaged with basketballs.

That was four years before Reese was born, meaning that a Black basketball-playing Barbie existed before Angel Reese did. Somehow, that didn't qualify as a doll that "looked like her" and could be a "killer on the court."

Her new doll doesn't mark the arrival of representation that had never existed. It marks another lucrative commercial opportunity for one of the most heavily promoted athletes in women’s sports.

Last month, I wrote about how frequently Reese presents herself as overlooked or unfairly treated, even as attention has helped make her one of the most famous and commercially successful players in women’s basketball.

ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND

Here's the truth: Angel Reese is incredibly privileged.

Reese attended St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, a private school where high school tuition is currently $15,000 per year. She was a McDonald's All-American and one of the top college recruits in the country.

She then played basketball at Maryland before transferring to LSU on a full scholarship, earning a free four-year college education and a bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Studies.

Now, she's a professional athlete with major endorsements, millions of social-media followers, a podcast, a signature shoe and a Barbie doll. She walked in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and attended the Met Gala for the third consecutive year in May.

And the preferential treatment hasn’t been limited to corporate America.

WNBA FANS CALL OUT GLARING DOUBLE STANDARD AFTER ANGEL REESE’S CLUELESS RESPONSE TO PAIGE BUECKERS BET

The Dream acquired Reese from Chicago in April for two first-round picks. The deal came only months after Reese publicly ripped the Sky’s roster, questioned her teammates and warned that she might have to "move in a different direction" if the organization didn’t improve.

Chicago suspended her for comments it deemed "detrimental to the team."

Yet, rather than suffer any real consequence for publicly bashing the organization that drafted her in the first round of the 2024 WNBA Draft, Reese landed with a ready-made contender willing to pay a premium price.

That team then made her the centerpiece of a major marketing campaign, including an entire game-night promotion built around her personal brand.

Most athletes never receive any one of those opportunities, let alone all of them.

Yet, sitting beside a doll made in her image during a night built around celebrating her brand, Reese focused on what the world had failed to give her.

At this point, victimhood no longer seems like an occasional theme in the Angel Reese story.

It looks like the brand.

item.title: Mets call up pitcher known for his over the top strikeout celebrations as dismal season hits new level
item.description: Mets pitcher Jefry Yan does splits and screams after every strikeout in the minors, and his dominant ERA earned him a reported call-up to the MLB.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets very comfortably occupy the basement of the National League East and are set to miss the postseason for the second consecutive year. A franchise living in that reality making a roster move would not garner any attention, but when that move involves a guy who does the splits after striking out hitters, an exception is made.

The Mets selected the contract of left-handed pitcher Jefry Yan on July 2, and hours after the MLB trade deadline officially passed on Aug. 3, Yan was among a handful of pitchers reportedly promoted.

Mets fans have nothing to look forward to in the immediate term, but watching Yan potentially make his debut in The Show may as well be appointment viewing.

BREWERS PITCHER ABNER URIBE APOLOGIZES AFTER CONTROVERSIAL STRIKEOUT CELEBRATION SPARKS BACKLASH

Beyond the 29-year-old's impressive numbers at both the AA and AAA levels in 2026, Yan puts on a show, in the most literal way, every time he takes the bump.

Jumping into the air, doing the splits, screaming at the top of his lungs, smacking the ground. You name it, Yan does it.

While his antics look like something straight out of a Savannah Bananas game, the dude can throw a baseball.

After bouncing around the Minor League systems of the Los Angeles Angels, Miami Marlins, and Colorado Rockies early in his career, Yan inked a deal with the Mets in August 2025, and 2026 has been a mighty kind year for the Dominican native.

In 26.2 innings of work with AA Binghamton, Yan posted a 3.71 ERA while striking out 45 batters. After taking the step up to AAA Syracuse, his stuff only got better.

In his 15.0 innings with Syracuse, Yan owns a record of 2-1, an ERA of 2.40 while giving up just six hits and striking out 32.

Do the jokes write themselves given that Yan plays for the punching bag of Major League Baseball? Yes. Will the Mets get clowned on social media when Yan gives up a home run or struggles after doing a Michael Jackson stunt on the mound? You bet.

On the flip side, at least Mets fans have something to talk about for a brief moment other than the team being 19 games below .500 in early August.

item.title: Tick-borne 'rabbit fever' spreads with cases reported near major metro area
item.description: Three probable tularemia cases on Long Island have officials warning residents about the tick-borne illness after a 9-year-old developed severe symptoms.
item.content:encoded:
Health officials on Long Island are warning residents about a rare but potentially serious tick-borne illness.

Three probable cases of tularemia — also known as "rabbit fever" — have been confirmed by the Suffolk County Department of Health Services (SCDHS).

"SCDHS currently has three probable cases of tularemia this year," the agency said in a statement provided to local outlets. "Confirmation of a tularemia diagnosis requires a combination of laboratory testing and fulfillment of specific clinical or epidemiologic criteria. The laboratory testing to confirm a tularemia diagnosis may take several weeks."

NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

One case involved a 9-year-old patient who was bitten by a tick while playing outside, according to NBC4 New York. After the tick was removed, he later developed high fever, severe head and neck pain, swollen lymph nodes/glands, body aches and extreme fatigue.

After multiple doctor visits and nearly a month of illness, an infectious disease specialist diagnosed the boy with tularemia.

Although the family's yard is home to wild rabbits, the patient's mother said he never handled the animals. Doctors believe infected ticks likely fed on the rabbits before biting the boy, transmitting the bacteria, according to reports.

Caused by the bacteria Francisella tularensis, the disease commonly infects rabbits, hares and rodents. However, it is zoonotic, which means it can spread from animals to humans.

The bacteria is a "tier-1 select agent," a classification given to agents and toxins that "present the greatest risk of deliberate misuse with significant potential for mass casualties or devastating effects to the economy, critical infrastructure or public confidence, and pose a severe threat to public health and safety," per the CDC.

TICK BITE ER VISITS HIT HIGHEST SEASONAL LEVEL IN YEARS AS DOCTORS WARN OF DISEASE SURGE

Although tularemia remains rare, with 196 U.S. cases reported in 2023, the disease has become more common in recent years. CDC surveillance found 2,462 cases between 2011 and 2022 — a 56% increase in incidence compared with the previous decade (2001–2010).

Daniel Ruderfer, M.D., chief of the Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Hackensack Meridian K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital in New Jersey, believes that the increase in cases is mostly due to improved microbiology detection methods.

"The traditional method of confirming cases has historically been via growth in culture and antibody testing," he previously told Fox News Digital.

"However, newer detection methods, such as PCR testing, are likely a major contributor to the increase in reported cases."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Humans can contract the disease through bites from deer flies or ticks, contact with infected animals, or exposure to contaminated water or aerosols, the same source stated.

Symptoms of tularemia can vary depending on the type of disease. General symptoms include chills, headache, malaise, fatigue, anorexia, myalgia, chest discomfort, cough, severe sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, according to Ruderfer.

"Depending on the location of the infected bit or scratch, people can develop localized lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes) and a cutaneous ulcer at the infection site," he said.

"Other manifestations include conjunctivitis, pneumonia and potentially even bloodstream infections."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The death rate from the disease is typically low, less than 2%, but the CDC noted that it can be as high as 24% in rare, severe cases.

Tularemia can be treated with antibiotics, but no vaccine is currently available.

"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics," said Ruderfer.

Those most at risk include children between 5 and 9 years of age, older men, American Indian and Alaskan Native people, and those living in central U.S. states, according to the report.

The general population is not at an "obvious" risk for infection unless they come into physical contact with an infected rabbit, tick or deer fly, the expert noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Those who hunt or interact routinely with rabbits should see a doctor if they develop any concerning symptoms, he advised.

"Many factors might contribute to the higher risk for tularemia in this population, including the concentration of Native American reservations in central states and sociocultural or occupational activities that might increase contact with infected wildlife or arthropods," the CDC wrote.

item.title: WNBA fan goes viral for half-court shot horror show that left him sprawled on the court
item.description: A Portland Fire fan's half-court shot attempt during the WNBA game against the Los Angeles Sparks barely cleared the free throw line area.
item.content:encoded:
Few things in sports can get a fan's nerves up like being told you get to take a half-court shot at an NBA or WNBA game for cash or a car.

Sure, you could, by some miracle, make the shot, but you're more likely to embarrass yourself in front of an arena full of people... at least the ones who are still in their seats and aren't in line for a beer or the bathroom.

But, at least we can all be sure that if you take a shot, the odds of it being a worse display than one put on by a Portland Fire fan over the weekend are very, very low.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT CAUGHT HITTING LAUGHABLY BAD GOLF SHOT AFTER ALLEGEDLY DITCHING INTERVIEW

The Fire (whose logo I only just realized is a flaming rose. Seriously, I've had an easier time decoding death metal band logos) have a half-court shot competition according to their website. It's sponsored by Toyota, meaning that draining the shot earns you a brand new Toyota.

Hopefully a Land Cruiser. Those are cool.

One fan got this golden opportunity on Sunday when the Fire took on the Los Angeles Sparks and... well, let's just say that Portland area Toyota dealers were not sweating it on this one.

Oh, dear God...

ATLANTA BRAVES FAN TAUNTS THE FREEZE WITH A BLOWN KISS AND GETS PASSED IN SPECTACULAR FASHION

Rule No. 1 of half-court shots should be that whatever you do, your biggest goal is to at least hit the backboard. I'd argue it's much better to airmail that ball into the club level seats than it is to barely get it past the free throw line.

That's a rough look as it is, but imagine putting every last drop of mustard you have on the ball to the point that you go scrawling across that flaming rose logo (seriously, did anyone else not pick up on that at first?). That tells the entire crowd in attendance you gave it your all... which is normally good, but that's not enough "all."

The big winner in all of this is that guy's glasses. Talk about a snug fit. Those things were on there!

That was maybe the only thing that went right for him. If those specs had gone clattering across the hardwood, I think he would've had to change his name, move out of Portland, and start rooting for a new WNBA team.

Luckily for him, he wasn't the only loser as the Fire fell to the Sparks that night 106-101.

item.title: French trans phenom Julie Tétart looks WNBA-ready — so why hasn’t the ‘inclusive’ league called?
item.description: Julie Tétart dominated French women's basketball with 21 points and 20 rebounds per game and says a WNBA call would mean time to talk business.
item.content:encoded:
French trans basketball player Julie Tétart is waiting for a call from one of the inclusive WNBA teams who needs a 6'3 scoring and rebounding machine.

During the 2025-26 season for a club team in Monaco, Tétart dominated the second-tier French women's basketball Ligue 2 by dropping 21 points per game while grabbing 20 rebounds. The biological male, who came out as trans in October 2021, led the league in both categories. It was as season unlike any the Ligue 2 had ever seen.

With those numbers, the WNBA should be knocking down Tétart's door, right?

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

"If they contact me, I won't say no. But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" the overly humble 34-year-old Tétart told OutKick in French over Instagram direct messages on Monday.

Far better? Are you sure?

Tétart's season was so dominant that French media was stunned when the shredded center didn't win league MVP honors. The season was still good enough to win Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year and Domestic Player of the Year.

Woke WNBA fans swear there's no clear and present trans danger to biological women. They swear this is some sort of delusion cooked up by MAGA.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

Meanwhile, Tétart destroyed Ligue 2 so badly that there were collusion allegations being made against league captains and coaches who voted on the MVP award.

Those same voters are alleged to have excluded 43-year-old trans player Aurore Pautou (14.4 PPG, 7.7 RPG) from winning postseason awards. French trans groups are furious. "Despite top-tier athletic performance on the court during the 2025/2026 season by Julie and Aurore, voters for the Ligue 2 Féminine de Basket Awards deliberately decided not to grant them any awards," activist group TRANSpire cried on Instagram.

Former WNBA player Audrey Sauret, who's French, spoke out in April after the MVP drama and sounded a warning to leagues around the world as to what's coming if they don't protect biological females.

"Ligue 2 serves as a kind of testing ground, to introduce trendy ideas, but by allowing them to participate in professional competitions, we create unfair competition, especially for younger players," Sauret wrote. "This can close doors and discourage aspiring athletes. This situation risks becoming commonplace, even if it’s regulated. Men and women aren’t built the same way. Changing hormones doesn’t erase gender differences. I regret that this issue wasn’t addressed much sooner."

TRANS ATHLETE WINS NEW YORK STATE GIRLS' SHOT PUT TITLE, BEATING SECOND PLACE BY MORE THAN 2 FEET

During a March game that should've been a trans showdown, Tétart had 21 points and 30 rebounds, which was a new league record, breaking the previous record of 25 rebounds (Tétart held that record, as well), but Pautou didn't play.

The question we had for Tétart was simple: Would you ever consider trying out for the inclusive WNBA? The trans scoring and rebounding machine seemed confused at first before realizing we were 100% serious.

"Obviously, it's a childhood dream just like for any female basketball player, but unfortunately, it's not possible," the French native wrote back.

Wait a minute, why not? The WNBA is inclusive. What are we missing here?

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"The league, yes. The country, no, haha," Tétart fired back while hinting at some sort of problem with Donald Trump's presidency.

When pressed on what would need to change politically in the U.S., Tétart stopped playing games with me, finally admitting that if a WNBA call came, it would be time to talk business: "I won't say no."

As for Sophie Cunningham's stance that biological males need to stay out of women's sports, I gave Tétart a chance to respond. "Aucun," the French stat stuffer replied.

Translation: "None."

Imagine a Tétart vs. Cunningham matchup in 2027. It's time for the WNBA to once and for all prove just how inclusive it is. Tétart's DMs are wide open.

item.title: Second lady Usha Vance gets candid about new baby, juggling four children and motherhood
item.description: Second lady Usha Vance reveals how her older children are reacting to the birth of new baby Alec — and why she's glad the family took the plunge despite having some initial angst.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: In her first interview since the birth of her fourth child with Vice President JD Vance just a few weeks ago, Usha Vance described the joy of being a new mother all over again during a candid interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday, August 4.

The interview came on the same day the newest episode of her popular podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady," was set to go live. 

"It's been really lovely so far," she said of the experience of having four children, speaking from the Vice President's Residence. "One of the things that has just been beautiful to see is how excited my older kids are about their new brother. They're always fighting over holding him. When we do diaper changes or clothes changes, one of them is always there helping. They're willing to burp him, they want to grab things for him, they want to entertain him."

JD VANCE AND WIFE USHA WELCOME FOURTH CHILD, REVEAL BABY BOY'S NAME

She added, "So there's this really great way in which their needs are complementary with his."

Vice President Vance and his wife announced the birth of their fourth child in a July 20 Instagram post, as Fox News Digital previously reported. The couple said their baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born on Sunday morning, July 19. 

"We are excited to announce that our baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born this morning," the couple wrote. "Usha and the baby are happy and healthy, and our kids are overjoyed to meet their little brother."

On Tuesday in her on-camera interview with Fox News Digital, Mrs. Vance called out the importance of doing things one on one with each of her children and the baby.

"They feel like they're getting their own personal time with both of us," she said. 

"For example, we go out [of the residence] and do something every day. And we've been doing that since the day we came home from the hospital. So yesterday was my middle child's day, and we went to a bookstore, we went to lunch — we did a quick return at a shop, and the whole time, it was just really special.

IVANKA TRUMP AND BETTINA ANDERSON'S CLOSE BOND ON DISPLAY AT MAR-A-LAGO BRIDAL SHOWER

"And we're trying to do that all the time. Now, I'm sure there are going to be hiccups here and there! But for right now, they seem to be really thriving."

She added, "My older kids see this as only good for themselves. Like, there's only one more kid to add to their pack. The parents are now outnumbered two to one!"

She referenced the jitters she had a bit ago — and how those were swiftly put to rest, and now part of the past.

"I would say I had all sorts of angst about this. My family [had] felt so complete. My kids were growing into a new phase," said Mrs. Vance. 

Now, she said, "I'm really glad that we took this plunge. I'm really glad that we decided to move into the unknown and do something that felt like a little bit of a risk to a settled and happy family dynamic because it's only become happier."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"And we're looking forward to seeing what the next few years bring."

She is also continuing to expand and develop her podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady."

The latest episode features author Jackie Oshry reading her children's book about summer camp. Mrs. Vance said the podcast is designed to encourage children not only to read books but also to imagine creating stories of their own.

"One of the things we're trying to do with this podcast is highlight authors of books to show [the children] that it's not just reading that you can do," she said. "You can imagine your own stories. You can write them yourself."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

So why this signature issue for her as second lady — and not others that she might have chosen? Mrs. Vance said that reading has long been one of her favorite hobbies and something she enjoys sharing with her own children. 

She said she chose literacy as one of her key initiatives because she wanted to make "a concrete change" while serving as second lady. She noted how critical it is that children in America develop a love of, and facility with, reading from a young age. 

She is also encouraging children in kindergarten through eighth grade to participate in the White House Summer Reading Challenge by reading 12 books before the end of August. Families who complete the challenge will be entered to win prizes — including a chance to visit the White House, she said.

In the waning weeks of summer, Mrs. Vance said her family is preparing for a new school year by gathering school supplies, organizing clothes and spending as much time outdoors as possible before classes begin for her older children.

"We're trying to make it a celebratory thing," she said of the family's back-to-school traditions. 

"Over the month of August, we slowly get everything prepared so it doesn't come as too much of a shock when they have to wake up at 6:30 again every morning."

President Donald Trump declared in a Truth Social post right after the Vances' new baby was born, "Congratulations! A perfect baby boy for the wonderful Vance family."

His post included a photo of the infant and two children.

item.title: The scam text test: Spot danger before you tap
item.description: A simple six-step scam text test helps you spot phishing messages about fake deliveries, toll notices and bank alerts before you click or share anything.
item.content:encoded:
Your phone buzzes. The text reads, "Your package is delayed. Confirm your address here." A little later, it's a text message about an unpaid toll, suspicious bank activity or an account that will be locked unless you act now.

That's how scam texts work. They don't always look wild or obviously fake. They look routine, urgent and easy to deal with in a hurry. The good news: You don't need to memorize every scam. You just need a quick way to test suspicious messages before you tap. Here's the simple scam text test to run before you click, pay or share anything.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE SHINYHUNTERS SEXTORTION EMAIL USES CARNIVAL BREACH DATA

If a text asks you to click, pay, verify, sign in or fix a problem, run through these checks first.

Are you actually waiting for that package? Do you use that bank? Did you recently drive on a toll road? If the answer is no, treat the message as suspicious. Even if the answer is yes, don't assume it's real. Scammers rely on coincidence. They send thousands of similar messages knowing that some recipients will be waiting for a package or use the company being impersonated.

Urgency is one of the biggest red flags. Watch for phrases like:

A real company may send an urgent alert, but scammers use pressure to stop you from checking whether the message is legitimate. Take a breath before responding. A few extra minutes spent verifying the message can prevent days or weeks of dealing with a stolen account.

Before tapping, check for:

Even if the address looks legitimate, avoid opening links in unexpected texts. Scammers can disguise links or create convincing copies of real websites. Verify the message through the company's official app or a website you type in yourself.

Many scam texts use vague greetings, odd wording, awkward punctuation or slightly incorrect brand names. You might see a message addressed to "Dear customer" instead of your name. It may refer to a package without showing an order number or claim to come from a bank without identifying the account involved. Good grammar doesn't guarantee a message is safe. Scammers now use artificial intelligence to write more convincing messages. Still, sloppy wording and missing details remain warning signs.

Be skeptical of any text asking for:

Legitimate companies may send you a one-time verification code. However, a bank, government agency or customer service representative should never ask you to give that code to someone else. Anyone who asks for your code may be trying to take control of your account.

This is the most important step. Instead of using the link or phone number in the message:

If the issue is real, you should still be able to find it through one of those trusted channels.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

Scam texts often fall into a few familiar categories.

These messages claim a package was delayed, an address needs to be corrected or a small shipping fee must be paid. The link may lead to a fake postal or delivery website that collects your card information, password or home address.

These texts claim someone used your card, your account has been locked or you must verify a transaction immediately. The message may include a phone number connecting you to a scammer pretending to work for the bank.

Toll scams claim you owe a small amount and will face a larger penalty if you don't pay immediately. The amount is often low enough to make paying seem easier than investigating. The payment page then steals your financial information.

These messages claim your email, payment app, streaming service or social media account will be suspended. They direct you to a fake login page designed to capture your username and password. These scams work because each message sounds plausible. The goal is to make you react first and think later.

Don't panic, but act quickly.

Simply opening a phishing page doesn't always mean your information was stolen. The risk increases if you entered information, downloaded a file or approved a permission request.

Use a different password for every important account. A password manager can create and store strong passwords so one stolen login doesn't give scammers access to everything else.

Change the affected account's password immediately and check whether a new device, email address or phone number was added. Contact the company through its official app, website or phone number. Tell the representative that someone may have gained access to your account.

Report any charges you don't recognize as soon as possible.

HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS

Visit IdentityTheft.gov to create a recovery plan. You may also want to place a fraud alert or security freeze on your credit files. A credit freeze can prevent criminals from opening many types of new accounts in your name.

Avoid entering sensitive information on the device until you are confident it is secure.

After securing your accounts:

Reporting scam texts helps phone carriers and government agencies identify active campaigns.

Good habits are your first line of defense, but strong antivirus software can add another layer of protection. Some security tools can warn you about suspicious links, phishing websites and malicious downloads before they put your information at risk.

Many text scams are only the first step. The message sends you to a fake website. That site may steal your password, payment details or other personal information. In some cases, it may also try to install malware on your device.

Look for security software that offers:

Security software cannot catch every scam or replace careful judgment. Still, it can help stop a suspicious link or malicious download before one quick tap leads to fraud or an account takeover. Features vary by provider and device, so check what is included before choosing a service.

You never have to solve a surprise text from inside the text. Stop, verify independently and only act through official channels. That one habit can help you avoid a huge number of text scams.

Scam texts work because they make an everyday problem feel urgent. A package delay, unpaid toll or bank warning can seem believable enough to make you tap without thinking. Don't use the link or phone number in the message. Open the company's official app, type its website yourself or call a number you already trust. Strong antivirus software can help flag some suspicious texts and fake websites, but no security tool catches everything. Taking a few seconds to verify the message can save you from a stolen account or a costly mistake.

item.title: Paul Finebaum’s proclamation about Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer reignites college football ‘culture fit’ debate
item.description: Paul Finebaum says Kalen DeBoer lacks the right ingredients to win a national championship at Alabama despite averaging top-three recruiting classes.
item.content:encoded:
I mentioned it a while back, but August is the only time of year when almost every college football fanbase feels like their team has a chance to win it all.

Hope does indeed spring eternal every summer, but there are still plenty of programs who realistically have no shot at even making a College Football Playoff appearance.

One juggernaut who has historically been among the "haves" rather than the "have nots" is the Alabama Crimson Tide, but according to college football commentator Paul Finebaum, Bama's days of owning the lion's share of championship trophies may have come to an abrupt halt.

And it's all thanks to the man they hired to fill the team-issued polo previously worn by Nick Saban.

DID ALABAMA DOOM THEMSELVES TO MEDIOCRITY WITH KALEN DEBOER EXTENSION?

"I'm selling that," Finebaum said on Crane & Co. when asked if he would "buy or sell" Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer winning a natty while in Tuscaloosa. "I'll spare you the 'I think Kalen DeBoer is a good football coach.' I think everybody does. The question is, 'is he going to win a championship at Alabama?' And my answer is no."

Finebaum goes on to call the "culture fit" between DeBoer and Bama "okay," and says Alabama is a unique job where sometimes really good football coaches don't necessarily win titles due to factors that go far beyond the painted lines of Bryant Denny Stadium.

"In the last 60 years, only three people have won national championships, two of them happen to be the greatest coach of all-time on the day they retired," Finebaum stated. "At Alabama, you can be unique, you can be different, but Kalen DeBoer, to me, just doesn't have the right ingredients to win the title there."

'HOT SEAT RANKINGS' FOR ALL 16 SEC COACHES AS BEGINNING OF 2026 COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON DRAWS NEARER

It's interesting to hear Finebaum say that DeBoer doesn't have the right "ingredients" to win at Bama, but if you know what he means by that, it makes a ton of sense.

"Ingredients," in this instance, doesn't refer to talent on the field, because DeBoer and his staff haven't exactly been lacking in that department.

In the three full offseasons that DeBoer has been the head coach at Alabama, his average recruiting class ranking according to the 247Sports composite has been 2.5.

Every coach in America can only dream of averaging a top-three recruiting class every year they've been at their current school, but it's more than just a talent issue.

IF YOU BELIEVE ALABAMA WASN'T RECRUITING JEREMIAH SMITH, YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND RECRUITING

As Finebaum mentioned, the "culture fit" wasn't right from the start between DeBoer and his current employer, and though that may sound like a nebulous excuse, there's some real weight behind it.

"He's capable of winning it elsewhere," Finebaum reasoned. "He came within a reasonable chance of winning it at Washington. I think he could probably have won one at Michigan. Alabama's different."

For those who don't remember, DeBoer was rolling while coaching the Washington Huskies.

In his two seasons in the Pacific Northwest, DeBoer had two top-ten finishes and a national championship appearance under his belt.

BY ADDING ED ORGERON TO STAFF, LANE KIFFIN AND LSU ADDRESS KEY FLAW FROM PREVIOUS REGIME

Even before he arrived at the ranks of the Power 4, DeBoer was a noted winner, capturing three NAIA National Championships while at Sioux Falls and guiding Fresno State to a nine-win regular season in just his second year there.

The point is, DeBoer didn't just forget how to coach the moment his plane touched down in Tuscaloosa, and it's not like he's been an abject failure for the Tide either.

Averaging ten wins a year and making a CFP appearance would be welcomed at 99% of schools in the country.

But as Finebaum said so poignantly, "Alabama is different."

CURT CIGNETTI REVEALS HOW WORKING FOR NICK SABAN CHANGED EVERYTHING: 'EVERY DAY WAS 4TH-AND-1'

It's the same reason a guy like Brian Kelly, a coach who went 145-61 in his three FBS stops prior to landing in Baton Rouge, "failed" at LSU.

Kelly is not a bad coach or even an average coach, but he didn't understand the culture and expectations that come with being the Tigers' head coach.

Will DeBoer prove everyone wrong and win a title at Bama? I can't say for sure.

As long as they keep recruiting at their current pace, a coach like DeBoer has a chance.

WHAT DOES A REALISTICALLY SUCCESSFUL FIRST YEAR LOOK LIKE FOR HEAD COACH LANE KIFFIN AT LSU?

But I also wouldn't be shocked to see him looking for a job in two to three years either.

Programs like Alabama and LSU have one goal and one goal only: to win a national championship.

And sometimes, even that isn't enough to save your job (see: Ed Orgeron).

DeBoer will be judged by the trophy case he assembles while coaching the Crimson Tide, and right now, that sucker is looking a little empty.

item.title: Kelly Osbourne demands child support and her dogs back in fiery rant amid reported breakup
item.description: The since-deleted posts escalate from cryptic accusations to demands for child support and possessions amid her reported split from Sid Wilson.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Osbourne appeared to take aim at her reported ex-fiancé, Sid Wilson.

The television personality sparked new questions about their relationship after posting a barrage of blistering Instagram Stories on Monday.

The since-deleted posts, viewed by Fox News Digital, appeared to accuse the musician of dodging accountability while vowing to put their son first.

KELLY OSBOURNE WELCOMES FIRST BABY WITH SID WILSON, SHARON OSBOURNE PRAISES DAUGHTER: 'SO PROUD'

Although Osbourne, 41, never mentioned Wilson by name, the timing and tone of the posts quickly raised questions about the pair's reported split.

One of her first messages took aim at someone she suggested was deflecting blame instead of accepting responsibility.

"Strange how the loudest defense of the guilty is rarely innocence... It's distraction. When the mask slips, they don't face the mirror they throw it at someone else. I also heard that when you break a mirror you get 7 years bad luck! Or is that just karma? This is why I always take accountability! As they say some are sicker then [sic] others," the post read.

Osbourne also reposted a quote that read, "My son's little heart once beat right beside mine. So trust me when I say... I will protect it at all costs," seemingly referring to the couple's 3-year-old son, Sidney.

In another message, she wrote, "Wake the f--- up and take some responsibility. I will not take your s--- anymore! I'm done. I want to be happy, and I have a beautiful son to raise. Leave me alone. Let me heal. I can't protect you from yourself anymore."

She later reposted another message about choosing children's well-being over everyone else's.

"My job is to protect my kids. Not your feelings. Not your expectations. Not judgments I didn't ask for. My responsibility is to protect their well-being. Their nervous systems. Their emotional safety. I will choose them every single time. Over anyone. Over anything."

Osbourne then appeared to reference unresolved issues involving possessions, finances and the care of their son.

"Also while I’m at it can I have my dogs back and all my possessions. Oh yeah and maybe some child support?"

Fox News Digital has reached out to Osbourne and Wilson for comment.

The cryptic posts add another chapter to the couple's reported breakup.

Osbourne and Wilson reportedly ended their engagement in March, about eight months after Wilson proposed, though neither has publicly confirmed the split.

The pair began dating in 2022 and welcomed their son, Sidney, later that year.

Meanwhile, Wilson has also faced career uncertainty in recent days.

SLIPKNOT’S SID WILSON SUFFERS SEVERE BURNS AFTER FARM EXPLOSION

The rocker was reportedly just fired from Slipknot after 28 years with the band, according to TMZ. The outlet reported the band had become fed up with Wilson's alleged behavior, particularly his treatment of fellow members.
